title: Mahabharata
author: vyasa
attributionNote: Traditionally attributed to Vyasa. The poem grew through oral and written transmission over centuries; the surviving text is a composite rather than a single authorial work.
description: The eighteen books of the Mahabharata: the rivalry of the Pandavas and Kauravas, the dice game and exile, the war at Kurukshetra, and the long instruction in dharma that follows it. The Bhagavad Gita is the best-known episode within the sixth book. Ganguli's complete prose translation is printed here in four volumes, with the printed section divisions indexed separately wherever the transcription preserves them.
historicalContext: Composed and transmitted between roughly the fourth century BCE and the fourth century CE, with later additions. The Ganguli translation (1883–1896) was the first complete English prose rendering and remains the standard public-domain one.
availabilityNote: Complete. All eighteen books of Ganguli's prose translation, streamed from four Project Gutenberg volumes at read time. The transcription divides the text into 1,892 numbered sections wherever it prints SECTION headings; Books 8–11 and 16–18 are printed as continuous text without them and are one navigable chapter each.
